verdicts.reason: A keeps the logo in its white header and the CTA reads clearly. But the headline, body and eyebrow are crammed together at the top, the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow now sits below the body copy, and a large dead gap separates the text from the rule and CTA. B jams the CTA into the white header against the logo, leaves the top half empty, and runs the orange rule straight through the body text ('gone until'). The eyebrow is also out of order.

In A the logo straddles the header/navy boundary so it looks cropped, and the headline has shrunk to near-body size. Its text block floats in the middle with a huge empty top, and a small CTA is stranded at the bottom. B (the same as in pair 1) has the CTA colliding with the logo in the header, the rule striking through the body copy, half the canvas dead, and the eyebrow under the body.

In A the white header is now empty and the logo has moved to the bottom, dark on navy and almost invisible, so the brand is effectively lost. 'Ships late June' is oversized and competes with the undersized CTA, and the eyebrow sits below the body. B has the CTA crammed against the logo, the rule cutting through the body copy, and a vast empty upper half.

In A the header band is empty and the logo is dropped to the lower left as a near-invisible dark mark on navy. The eyebrow sits below the body, the rule floats under the CTA, and the bottom third is dead space. Still, the text and CTA form a readable group. B has the CTA jammed into the header against the logo, the rule striking through the body text, and a large empty top half.
